questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the University was placed in a student friendly city. Lund is known for being a studentcity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: My host University (Lund University) made it super easy. Upon arrival they send a long letter with key information that would be relevant for upcoming exchange students. Among these links to accommodation sites, student organizations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival one could get assigned a mentor group. In this mentor group voluntary students arranged different social activitetes for the newly arrived exchange students. I found it was really useful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not hard. Upon arrival Lund University shared links to student accommodation sites, such as Bostaden.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Lund is a little, but friendly town. The locals are used to foreigners and are good at speaking English.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the first day, Lund University set up at registration event that was open the whole day. So you could just show up and register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could visit a reception on campus. The reception had normal office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of my first priorities, so really succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lund University sends out a lot of e-mail upon arrival, so you just have to keep updated in your mailbox.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was very high. A lot of the teachers are researchers for the University as well, so it was clear that they had a high passion and level of knowledge in their respective area.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There weren't as much group work. I didn't have any lectures (forelæsninger), so it reminded a lot of the seminars that we normally have in KUA.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Migration Law, Enviromental Climate Change Law, Business and Human Rights Law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Migration Law and Business and Human Rights Law

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Student membership for the different studentorganisations (nations), but it is a small amount of money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the food was pretty cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many social activités. Lund is a student city with a lot of student organisations. I could both join an athletic team, go to free yoga classes and attend parties almost every day of the week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring Malmø and Gøteborg. I went as a tourist. You get to experience the different nuances of Sweden just by visiting other cities. And also get the chance to see a lot of beautiful nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Lund is a student city, so it seemed like the locals were fairly used to foregniers. They were friendly and spoke a great deal of English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student organisations! You get to meet a lot of local students!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience any cultural differences. Maybe because I am Danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika (coffee and cake) and 1. of may which is a big deal in Sweden!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is very cheap to live there and eat out - which is pretty great when you are used to Danish prices.

Lund is an amazing student city that attracts students from all over the world. It makes it easy to connect with people from all around the world!

You will taste the best cinnamon bun in Lund! (Fika)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I can't think of any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people that you get to meet. I got the change to become friends with young people from all around the world. I was surprised how easy it was to connect with people from a completely different background than yourself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was the weather. I went in the spring semester and a lot of the months were cold.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
